channel.description: Recent content in Reflection on Stephanie Tess van Slyck

item.title: Where MCP Would Fit in a Project Like Standflow
item.description: Model Context Protocol is not a replacement for a REST API. A short reflection on what it is, and where it would actually belong in a system I have already built.

item.title: The Excursion I Missed, and Building for a Place I Had Not Seen
item.description: The class visited the customer site. I could not attend, so this is about building for a context I only knew second-hand, and where the project stands.

item.title: The Legal and Ethical Side
item.description: The EU AI Act puts educational assessment in the high-risk category, which lands directly on the rubric assessor I built. Plus copyright in RAG, and the energy cost nobody sees.

item.title: Building a Whole Project with a Code Agent
item.description: I used an AI code agent to take over and finish an entire group project, Standflow. This is the honest version: what the agent did, what I kept for myself, the guardrails that made it safe, the near-disaster, and what actually makes agentic development work.

item.title: Specs as the Theory Behind the Code
item.description: Peter Naur argued the real product of programming is the theory the programmers hold, not the code. Working with a code agent makes that argument louder.
